answer: Retrospective Burst-Cluster Audit: each identity leaves a relic of arrival timestamps, and the system clusters new identities by arrival burst. If a burst exceeds a baseline rate, all members are flagged and must forge independent behavioral histories over a probation window before full privileges. An attacker then pays the cost of sustaining each clone separately through that window, and flagged bursts face a tide of delayed rewards that erodes the payoff of mass registration.
